item.text: {"question_id":"3B.9","answer":"During 2023, crisis response was materially mixed and generally insufficiently restrained. Tshisekedi chaired planning with FARDC, MONUSCO, and the EAC force for ceasefire, disarmament, and civilian protection, ordered mixed army-police patrols for the Francophonie Games, and convened an evaluation of the state of siege; the government also reported legal protections, inquiries, camp policing, and victim-access measures. These records establish presidential or governmental initiatives, but not adequate implementation, exposure-based resource allocation, or protective outcomes (BATCH-0021-E001; BATCH-0018-E001; BATCH-0021-E012; BATCH-0011-E003). The humanitarian burden remained severe: 6.8 million people were internally displaced by year-end; renewed eastern fighting displaced more than 450,000 people in October–November, left remote areas with little or no aid, and brought national displacement to 6.9 million; more than 25 million people faced crisis or emergency food insecurity amid conflict, infrastructure and investment constraints, and a $629.6 million WFP funding shortfall. These outcomes demonstrate exposure and resource pressure but do not by themselves establish Tshisekedi’s personal causation (BATCH-0010-E003; BATCH-0013-E014; BATCH-0022-E013). In Kwamouth, intercommunal violence killed at least 300 people and displaced more than 50,000; provincial security forces were not reinforced until September and assistance was inadequate. The government-level failure is relevant, but personal presidential ordering or approval is not shown (BATCH-0011-E001). In Goma, provincial military authorities—not a demonstrated presidential order—planned and directed Operation Keba; orders framed protesters as enemy auxiliaries, and security forces killed dozens, injured many, arbitrarily arrested civilians, and used torture or ill-treatment. The operation was under Governor Ndima’s provincial command, while the broader militarized approach and Republican Guard structure were associated with Tshisekedi’s government; specific presidential approval remains unproved (BATCH-0011-E018; BATCH-0011-E019; BATCH-0011-E022). The government announced an investigation, trials, treatment for injured people, and no impunity, while Amnesty found the investigation incomplete and reported contested collective prosecutions and inadequate remedy; four officers were convicted, but the excerpt does not establish full accountability or presidential corrective action (BATCH-0023-E014; BATCH-0011-E018; BATCH-0011-E022). Tshisekedi’s December rhetoric promised continued fighting, denounced M23 as terrorists, and urged enlistment; its causal effect on domestic harm is unproven, while ACLED reported that ceasefires temporarily reduced hostilities before October fighting resumed and that support for non-state armed groups risked arming future adversaries (BATCH-0007-E013; BATCH-0027-E006). Overall, the evidence supports recurring or widespread crisis-protection failures with partial formal and corrective measures, but not a finding that Tshisekedi personally ordered the Goma killings, caused all humanitarian outcomes, or established systematic nationwide terror.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E001","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0011-E019","BATCH-0011-E022","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0022-E013","BATCH-0010-E003"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0021-E001","BATCH-0018-E001","BATCH-0021-E012","BATCH-0011-E003","BATCH-0023-E014","BATCH-0007-E013","BATCH-0027-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Implementation and outcomes of presidential plans, patrols, legal measures, and the state-of-siege review are not consistently independently verified.","National humanitarian and displacement outcomes have multiple causes and do not isolate Tshisekedi’s responsibility.","Kwamouth response failures are attributed to the government, but personal presidential notice, approval, or corrective action is not shown.","Goma operational orders and alleged failures to prevent or remedy abuses are principally attributed to Governor Ndima and provincial commanders; presidential approval of the specific orders is unproved.","The government’s investigation and convictions provide partial corrective evidence, but independence, completeness, civilian remedy, and higher-level accountability remain contested.","The supplied evidence does not establish collective punishment or censorship as a nationwide presidential policy, nor a direct causal effect of Tshisekedi’s rhetoric on violence."],"corrections_made":["Added the full-year displacement, late-2023 access, food-insecurity, and WFP funding-shortfall evidence with multi-causal attribution.","Corrected Goma attribution by distinguishing Tshisekedi’s broader national militarized strategy from Ndima’s provincial orders and command responsibility.","Reduced positive weight assigned to official planning and reported protective mechanisms because implementation and outcomes are not established.","Preserved the government’s announced investigation, treatment, trials, and officer convictions as partial contrary or corrective evidence.","Clarified that the evidence supports materially adverse crisis management without proving presidential personal ordering of the Goma operation or nationwide systematic terror."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Further evidence could materially change attribution if it establishes Tshisekedi’s notice, approval, direction, or obstruction of remedy concerning Goma or Kwamouth.","Independent evidence of actual resource allocation by population exposure and humanitarian outcomes is incomplete.","The completeness and independence of Goma investigations, prosecutions, appeals, and victim remedies remain unresolved."]}
